answer: Each day the watcher changes the seismograph drum and files the trace under the station's own date, building a record no one can backdate. A lagoon trace drawn by hand fails the record: at the ocean of the drum the needle must have moved exactly as the ground shook, and a drawn line is too smooth. Faking a month of traces means running a station for thirty days, bribing a watcher and paying 16,100, while the hollow file in the observatory is read at every inspection, so a trace whose drum was never changed is thrown out.
